title: Paper bags and packing a purchase
summary: In Supermarket Simulator a paper bag is something the game builds and fills rather than a decoration standing on the counter: there is a factory that makes bags, a mode for placing one, and a record of which goods ended up inside it.
body: A bag is built, not painted in. The game has a factory that brings paper bags into the shop, and a mode of its own for placing one, which is why a bag can be brought out where it is wanted rather than only ever standing in a spot that was built into the scene.

What goes into a bag is remembered. A product that has been put in a bag is its own object rather than the loose product you see on a shelf, and there is a bag form of a product too, so the game can tell goods that are packed from goods that are not.
A bag belongs to an order. There is a bag for orders, a data object for it and a container that holds them, so a paper bag is not just a shape on the counter: it is the thing an order is carried in.
The packed bag exists in more than one place. It has a shared form and a form of its own for orders placed online, which is how a bag that has been filled is not only a local object on one machine.
Packing is an action with a shape. Filling a bag has an animation of its own, so it is a step with a beginning and an end that the game plays rather than an instant transfer of goods.

The counter around it is modelled too. There is a belt along the counter with a grid of its own, a drawer, and a manager for change, and the bag's placing mode fits into that arrangement instead of replacing it.
What this entry does not tell you: how many bags a shop gets through in a day, what paper costs, or how many goods fit in one bag. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: A paper bag is built by the game rather than placed in the shop as decoration.
There is a mode of its own for placing a bag.
A product that is in a bag is its own object, and there is a bag form of a product as well.
A bag belongs to an order, with its own data and a container of them.
The packed order bag has a shared form and a form for online orders.
Packing a bag has an animation of its own.
The counter is modelled as a belt with a grid, a drawer and a manager for change.
